title: Perform Post-slaughter Procedures for Beef Carcasses

lessons.title: Washing, inspection and marking
lessons.html:
What are post-slaughter procedures?

These are the jobs done after the carcass has been dressed and split, until it leaves the abattoir: final trimming and washing, helping at inspection, weighing and marking, chilling, and dispatch. In this module you practise these jobs.

Final trimming and washing

  1. Look over both sides of the carcass from top to bottom.
  2. Trim off any hair, dung, ingesta, bruises, blood clots and loose pieces with a sterilised knife. Put trimmings in the correct bin.
  3. Wash the carcass at the wash station, from the top down, with clean water. Do not use the hose to remove dung; trim it.
  4. Do not touch the carcass with dirty hands or aprons.

At the inspection point

  • Make sure the carcass, head and offal of each animal carry the same number.
  • Present the carcass so the inspector can see all sides; turn it if asked.
  • Follow the inspector's instructions exactly, for example to trim a part or move the carcass to the detention rail.
  • Never remove an inspection stamp, detention tag or ticket.

Weighing and marking

  1. Push the carcass onto the rail scale gently and wait for the reading to settle.
  2. Record the mass with the carcass number, or check the printed ticket.
  3. Attach the ticket or label in the right place.
  4. Check that the classification mark and inspection stamp are present.

Double-check numbers. A swapped label means the wrong farmer is paid, and the carcass cannot be traced if there is a problem with the meat later.

Safety

Carcass sides are heavy. Push them along the rail at walking speed, keep your fingers away from the rollers and hooks, and never stand in front of a moving side.

lessons.title: Chilling, dispatch and cleaning up
lessons.html:
Moving carcasses into the chiller

  • Move carcasses into the chiller promptly after weighing.
  • Space the sides so they do not touch each other or the walls.
  • Fill the chiller in the order your supervisor gives, so the oldest stock goes out first.
  • Keep detained carcasses in the detention chiller or area, apart from passed carcasses.
  • Close the chiller door behind you every time.
  • Read the chiller thermometer at the times set and write the temperature on the record sheet. Report a high reading at once.

Before dispatch

  1. Check the dispatch order: which carcasses, how many, and for which customer.
  2. Check the truck: it must be clean, without smells, and cold before loading. Report a dirty or warm truck.
  3. Wear clean protective clothing and a hair net when loading.

Loading

  • Hang carcasses on the truck rails. Never put them on the floor of the truck.
  • Do not let carcasses touch the dirty outside of the truck or the ground when moving them across.
  • Load quickly and close the doors between loads to keep the truck cold.
  • Count the carcasses and sign the dispatch note with the driver.

If a carcass falls

Stop. Do not just hang it back. Tell the supervisor, who will get the meat inspector to decide what must be trimmed or done.

Cleaning up

At the end of the shift, clean the wash stations, scales and chiller floors following the cleaning schedule: dry clean, rinse, detergent, rinse, sanitise. Put bins in their places and report broken equipment.

Key points

  • Trim before washing and keep carcass, head and offal numbers matched.
  • Never remove stamps, detention tags or tickets.
  • Space carcasses in the chiller and record temperatures.
  • Load only clean, cold trucks, with carcasses hanging.
  • If a carcass falls, stop and report; the inspector decides.

quiz.question: How should dung on a carcass be removed?

options.text: Trim it off with a sterilised knife

quiz.question: What must match for each animal at inspection?

options.text: The colour of the carcass and the head
The numbers on the carcass, head and offal

quiz.question: What should you do if a carcass falls on the floor?

options.text: Stop and tell the supervisor so the inspector can decide
Wash it and send it out

quiz.question: What should you do if the truck is warm and dirty?

options.text: Report it and do not load

quiz.question: How should carcasses be loaded onto a truck?
Chiller temperatures should be read and recorded at the set times.
Workers may remove a detention tag if the carcass looks fine.
